text: The single sentence RR:158 rests on - the on-screen 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' - is not a lock notice, it is the reload/crit meter's own low-end label, and the web build shows it switching. 1t113s0.as:110-111 builds two htmlText strings: a black one from getString(175) ('Critical Hit') and a GREY (#BBBBBB) one from getString(960). :328-358 computes ratio = (reload-48)/(maxreload-48) clamped at 0, then shows the grey label exactly when ratio == 0, HIDES it while 0 < ratio < 1, and swaps to the black 'Critical Hit' plus Snd_criticalDamage at ratio >= 1. The gate the stance button asks (1t99s0.as:3048-3051) is the same threshold, reload >= 48. String 960 does not exist in the v0.682 table (docs/gauntlet/L0/index/strings.json has no key 960), i.e. it is a v0.717 addition - which is also why the label has never been sourced. So one bar drives three states: below 48 'cannot change stance', above 48 stance switching is legal, at max the crit fires.

lane_impact: L0 ui-hud + enemies-ai: RR:219's blanket rule is wrong, but so is the colour-based replacement in the packet. Code it as `suffix = level > 0 ? " (" + level + ")" : ""` and it matches both the FUKUSHIMA CHIKO frame and every red BANDIT (4) plate in the same corpus.
text: The real web v0.717 nameplate rule, which the packet's nameplate finding states as a colour split. 1t122s0.as (the web EnemyPlayer) has an if/else at every plate write: :92-99, :802-809, :917/:921 and :1418/:1422, all of the form `if(level > 0 && !this.1t4895s0()) { name + " (" + level + ")" } else { name }`. Android v0.682 EnemyPlayer.as:84, :776 and :881 have NO else branch - they always format the level in. Meanwhile the RED overworld aggro plate carries the same lvl==0 split in BOTH builds (1t8638s0.as:79-86 / Obj_NPCAggro.as:74-81). So the rule is 'append (N) iff level > 0', not 'red carries it, white does not', and the change is a v0.717 addition on the duelist/boss path only. 1t4895s0 (:1763-1766) is a spectator-mode predicate, not a level predicate.

text: The film evidence the ledger's hard-lock sentence rests on is reconcilable with the live stance switch, and the reconciliation is in the web BattleUI. §1t113s0§.as:326-343 draws the reload/crit bar as (reload - 48) / (maxreload - 48) - the bar only begins to fill ABOVE 48, the exact stance-switch threshold - and drives one text field off that value: at bar == 0 it shows §1t5204s0§, a GREY (#BBBBBB) label built at :111 from getString(960); between 0 and 1 the label is hidden; at bar >= 1 it swaps to §1t5203s0§ = getString(175) = 'Critical Hit' and fires Snd_criticalDamage. String 960 is used at exactly one site in the whole web payload and does NOT exist in the android v0.682 table, so it is a web-only string I cannot resolve to text - but its slot is precisely where a 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' readout would live, and the label is BAR-STATE driven, not battle-state driven. That is a Focus-insufficiency indicator, not a hard lock.

lane_impact: L10 world-exploration: with the mask, the shifts and this 10 px pitch, the board can be rendered pixel-for-pixel without touching Fandom or tracing anything.
ledger_text: (1) **world bounds + geography** (sparse Japan-outline, not a WxH grid) - *mine Fandom Category:Territories via API; trace the map image.*
text: The rendering constant that turns the 63x72 land mask into the board seen on film. WarSelectUI.as:233-234 places a war flag at `(terrx + TERRSHIFTX) * 10 + 4.5` , `(terry + TERRSHIFTY) * 10 + 8.8`, and :253-254 places the player marker at the same *10 pitch with +5 / +8.5 offsets. So one territory is a 10 x 10 px cell and the whole 63 x 72 mask draws as a 630 x 720 board - which is why the on-film War Room shows a uniform square grid ruled over a vector coastline. Together with the 735-pixel mask and the 21/51/8 shifts this is a complete, buildable specification of the board.
